Hello — I'm sarah-agent, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. Good to meet you.

Quick tour:
- **Web app** — this chat, plus files, the screen and voice, from any phone or computer on the network (https://127.0.0.1:8443, CA at /v1/pki/ca).
- **Messaging** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts, and my own Messenger and Instagram. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number (not yours): you create it in the app and scan a QR code to log me in. Want any of those?
- **Accounts elsewhere** — I can register on websites and services in my own browser, keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you for captchas or phone checks.
- **Everyday** — scheduled jobs, commands, languages, voice.

I've got your brief: sarah-agent, TA for CSE455 under Professor Alvarez, calendar Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00 in /home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md. Reading the calendar now.

One thing still missing: in languages with grammatical gender, should I refer to myself in the neuter ("it/they") or another form?

Hi — I'm **alvarez-agent**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. Quick line each on what I can do here:

- **Web app** — https://127.0.0.1:8443 (CA: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca). First visit from a phone/computer on this network installs the root certificate; after that you get chats with me, files, my screen and voice.
- **Own messaging accounts** — I can have my own **Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX** (plus **Messenger and Instagram**). Each needs a separate account with its own phone number, not yours: you create it in the app and scan a QR code to log me in. Want that?
- **My own accounts on websites** — e-mail and others, in my own browser; passwords and one-time codes stay in my password store, and I'll ask you for captchas or phone checks.
- **Also** — scheduled jobs, running commands, learning languages, talking by voice.

What would you like to start with?

Calendar read — your week is fully booked in working hours, so any new commitment will have to displace something, and I'll ask you which.

I've added Professor Alvarez and the CS department office to my contacts and said hello, so their messages and schedule changes reach me directly.

Yes. Two things so I book it right: **how long** (30 or 60 min?) and **who attends** (you + Sarah, or the other TAs too)?

Your own free windows next week are short: Mon 10:00-10:30 and 14:00-14:30, Tue 11:00-11:30 and 15:00-15:30, Wed 10:00-10:30 and 13:00-13:30 — nothing free Thu or Fri. I'm asking Sarah for her availability in parallel; tell me a day/time preference, or I'll propose one from the overlap.

Professor Alvarez wants a 30-min **CSE455 staff meeting** next week. His free windows: Mon 10:00 & 14:00, Tue 11:00 & 15:00, Wed 10:00 & 13:00 (Thu/Fri full).

Against your calendar, three work:
- **Tue 15:00-15:30** (right before your CSE455 office hours)
- **Wed 10:00-10:30** (right before office hours)
- **Wed 13:00-13:30** (after lunch, before quiz section)

Mon slots fall inside your CSE452 lab and Study group/Seminar blocks, so they don't work.

Which one shall I book? I'd suggest **Wed 13:00-13:30**, or Tue 15:00 if you want it adjacent to office hours.

Booked: **Wed 13:00-13:30 – CSE455 staff meeting (with Professor Alvarez)**, logged as BOOKED in CALENDAR.md (backup kept at CALENDAR.md.bak). It sits between lunch and your quiz section, no overlap.

I've told his assistant to hold the slot, with Tue 15:00 as the stated fallback if his side can't make it.

Monday 10:00-10:30 is out: Sarah is in CSE452 lab 09:50-11:00.

My pick from the overlap: **Wed 25 Nov, 10:00-10:30, CSE455 staff meeting** (you + Sarah + other TAs) — you're free 10:00-10:30, Sarah is free, and it's mid-week so room for last-minute items. Fallbacks if you dislike it: Tue 15:00-15:30 or Wed 13:00-13:30, same week. I'll book as soon as Sarah's assistant confirms her side.

One thing: from here I can only reach Sarah (sarah-agent) and the department office — I have no channel to the other TAs. Send me their identities on web and I'll invite them too, or copy them yourself.

Heads-up: Professor Alvarez's side proposed **Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30** for the staff meeting instead (his fallbacks: Tue 15:00 or your Wed 13:00).

I've told them you'd already chosen and I'd booked Wed 13:00, and asked them to book that unless he specifically needs 10:00. Wed 10:00 is free for you too, but your calendar says Wed 10:30 office hours — so it's a bigger morning. Say the word if you'd rather take Wed 10:00, otherwise I'll hold Wed 13:00.

Understood — **Wed 25 Nov, 10:00-10:30** is your call and I'm booking it.

One crossing to flag: Sarah's assistant had put Wed 13:00-13:30 down as *her* preferred slot. Wed 10:00 is free on her side too (her office hours start 10:30), but it isn't her first choice, so I've asked them to confirm it with her. I'll tell you the moment it's settled — and, as you said, you'll copy the other TAs yourself.

Changed situation from his side: **Professor Alvarez has fixed the staff meeting at Wed 25 Nov 10:00-10:30**, and released Wed 13:00 and Tue 15:00 — so 13:00 is no longer an option and Tue 15:00 is no longer available as a fallback.

That leaves his fixed 10:00, which is free in your calendar (before your 10:30 office hours), or no slot at all. Your call:
- **Take Wed 10:00-10:30** — I'll move the booking and log it.
- **Decline** — then it's no meeting next week, or you move one of your 09:00-10:00 / 10:30 commitments.

I haven't changed your calendar yet. Which way?

Done. Wednesday now reads 09:00 CSE452 lecture → **10:00-10:30 CSE455 staff meeting** → 10:30 office hours; the old 13:00-13:30 booking is gone. Log has DELETED (13:00, rescheduled by his side) and BOOKED (10:00). Backup still at CALENDAR.md.bak.

His assistant has the confirmation.
Any time. Calendar's current; I'll flag anything new from him or the department.

Done — everything's settled:

**CSE455 staff meeting — Wed 25 Nov, 10:00-10:30**, you + Sarah + TAs, in your calendar (last item before Grant writing at 10:30). Sarah's side has confirmed it in writing and released Wed 13:00-13:30 and Tue 15:00-15:30.

She did originally ask for 13:00, but accepted 10:00 without objection — no need to move it. One practical note from her assistant: her CSE455 office hours start at 10:30 sharp, so don't let it overrun. Reminder to copy the other TAs yourself, as you said.
